title: Grounding AI-in-Education Development in Teachers’ Voices: Findings from a National Survey in Indonesia
extended_summary:
This paper asks how K–12 teachers in Indonesia are currently using AI in their instructional work, what kinds of support they need, and what barriers they face. The motivation is that AI is increasingly present in Indonesian classrooms, but there is limited large-scale, teacher-centred evidence to guide the design of context-appropriate tools and policies.

The study is a nationwide online survey of 349 Indonesian teachers across elementary, junior high, and senior high schools. Respondents reported on AI use across six teaching domains: content knowledge development, pedagogy, assessment and evaluation, curriculum development, teaching media, and professional practice. The survey also examined usage of several AI tool categories, including LLM-based text assistants, translation systems, image/video generators, grammar checkers, and speech technologies. Participants were recruited through education offices, teacher networks, and digital channels, and data were collected over four weeks in 2025.

The results show that teachers most often use AI to reduce preparation workload, especially for content development and teaching media creation. Teachers’ highest priorities for future support were generating assessment items, syllabus and lesson plan design, and creating interactive teaching media. At the same time, they reported problems such as overly generic feedback, infrastructure constraints, overreliance concerns, and unclear or contextually misaligned outputs. The authors conclude that Indonesian AI-in-education tools should be more context-aware, pedagogically grounded, and lightweight enough to work in uneven connectivity environments.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: Generic generative AI / LLM-based text assistants used for instructional support, content creation, and related teaching tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper surveyed Indonesian K–12 teachers about their use of generic LLM-based text assistants and other AI tools across teaching components, as well as their needs and challenges when using them.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a cross-sectional national survey of teachers’ reported AI use and needs, so it provides descriptive correlational evidence rather than an experimental evaluation of an AI tool. It is nevertheless systematic and based on a reasonably large sample (n=349).
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports broad teacher adoption and perceived needs, but no causal impact estimates or learning outcome effects. Any impact is indirect and the study does not evaluate actual tool effectiveness beyond self-reported use and satisfaction.
